goals.scientificAndAtomicityReason: Amount of substance counts explicitly specified entities in mole packages; mass is a separate quantity.
Molar mass unifies formula-based mass sum and m/n with formula indices and units; no bare substitution claim.
Atomic-scale u and bulk-scale g are distinguished by scale and particle count; rounded numeric molar-mass correspondence is not a newly exact SI identity.
NA is a proportionality constant with inverse-mole unit, and formula units/molecules/atoms must be specified.
Avogadro gas-volume claim means equal T and p in the ideal-gas approximation; no equal-mass or universal real-gas claim.
Vm=V/n is tied to specified T and p, not a universal constant value.
Molar mass of a pure gas links composition to rho*Vm at matching conditions, with unit and gas-model boundaries.
Selected gases such as H2, N2 and O2 are molecular and diatomic; notation and atomic conservation explain their equation use. No all-gas claim.
C/H presence is interpreted from controlled combustion-product tests; controls matter, and positive products do not establish unique hydrocarbon composition or exclude other elements.

Equation derivation is the same conserved chemical description across molecular and partial/overall representations. EN lacks the already claimed DE partial/overall clause; exact current BY10 clause supports alignment. Coefficients balance atoms/charges without altering substance indices.

excludedHeldGoals.reason: Independent ionic-property competence must be preserved as real same-scope target before narrower salt-formula adoption.

Relative-atomic-mass versus molecular-formula source scope and current BY9-other exact mapping require targeted resolution; separate two-goal followup, not silently certified by this ten-goal package.
